design.quote: Patients with HFrEF were randomized to receive placebo or 10 mg/day of empagliflozin.

population.value: Patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF)
population.quote: Patients with HFrEF were randomized to receive placebo or 10 mg/day of empagliflozin.

sample_size.quote: A total of 3,730 patients were included.

intervention.quote: Patients with HFrEF were randomized to receive placebo or 10 mg/day of empagliflozin.

comparator.quote: Patients with HFrEF were randomized to receive placebo or 10 mg/day of empagliflozin.

follow_up.quote: The median follow-up time was 16 months.

primary_findings.quote: The effect of empagliflozin (vs placebo) on the study primary outcome was more pronounced at lower baseline serum magnesium levels (Q1 HR: 0.54 mmol/L [95% CI: 0.41-0.71 mmol/L]; Q2 HR: 0.69 mmol/L [95% CI: 0.50-0.96 mmol/L]; Q3 HR: 0.82 mmol/L [95% CI: 0.58-1.15 mmol/L]; Q4 HR: 0.99 mmol/L [95% CI: 0.72-1.37 mmol/L]; and Q5 HR: 0.87 mmol/L [95% CI: 0.65-1.17 mmol/L], Pinteraction = 0.043).
primary_findings.outcome: Composite of cardiovascular death or heart failure hospitalization (primary outcome)

primary_findings.quote: Empagliflozin rapidly increased magnesium levels by 0.05 mmol/L.
The relative odds of experiencing lower magnesium levels were reduced with empagliflozin.
